extracted.intended_audience: Researchers, companies, nonprofits, and other applicants seeking CMEI (DOE Office of Critical Minerals and Energy Innovation) funding, prizes, or competitions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural/selection standards for applicants to the DOE Office of Critical Minerals and Energy Innovation funding, prize, and competition opportunities. Covers how funding is awarded, evaluation priorities, and where to find solicitations and deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open, competitive process / Funding Opportunity Exchange
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding is awarded through an open, competitive process hosted primarily on the Funding Opportunity eXCHANGE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should use the Funding Opportunity eXCHANGE to find current and past CMEI solicitations and to submit applications; different opportunities may have concept paper, full application, or phased submission requirements and specific open/close dates listed on that portal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit-based project selection
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects are evaluated on merit; applicants should ensure proposals demonstrate strong technical merit, feasibility, and value relative to competing submissions. The site emphasizes that selections prioritize projects offering clear benefits (see related benefit criteria).

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on potential energy, environmental, and economic benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Project selections place an emphasis on potential energy, environmental, and economic benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should clearly articulate how the project will produce energy benefits (e.g., cost reduction, performance improvements), environmental benefits (e.g., reduced emissions, ecosystem protection), and economic benefits (e.g., job creation, reduced system costs). Demonstrate measurable or credible pathways to these benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with DOE statutory mission, Administration and DOE policies
rubrics_metrics.description: DOE evaluates funding opportunities to ensure initiatives are in line with the statutory mission of DOE and the policies and priorities of the Administration and DOE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should align with DOE's stated mission and current policy priorities; applicants should review program goals and administration priorities and explain how their project supports them. Non-aligned projects may be deprioritized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with laws, regulations, and fiscal responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: DOE undertakes evaluation in accordance with all laws, regulations, and fiscal responsibility to ensure appropriate resources are allocated efficiently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must comply with applicable legal and regulatory requirements and justify the proposed budget and use of funds with clear fiscal responsibility. Demonstrate efficient use of requested funds and any cost-share or justification required by the solicitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programmatic goals: lower cost, reduce private-sector financial risk, and build resilient integrated energy systems
rubrics_metrics.description: CMEI invests in R&D to lower the cost of energy technologies, protect the private sector from financial risk, and help America build and sustain an integrated energy system that is reliable, resilient, and secure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should explicitly address one or more of these program goals: show how the work lowers technology costs, reduces commercialization or deployment risk for industry partners (financial de‑risking), and contributes to a reliable, resilient, and secure energy system. Provide metrics or plans that demonstrate impact toward these objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow program-specific submission formats and phases (concept papers, full applications, phased prizes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Opportunities may require different submission types (e.g., concept papers, full applications, phased prize entries) with specific open and close dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully follow the solicitation's required submission type, format, and deadlines (concept paper vs. full application vs. prize phase). Missing the correct phase or deadline can render an application ineligible; consult the Funding Opportunity eXCHANGE listing for each opportunity's exact requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use topic-specific guidance and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Find funding by topic (e.g., solar, wind, geothermal, vehicles, bioenergy, advanced materials & manufacturing, industrial technologies, hydrogen) and consult topic pages for further details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should review the topic-specific pages and resources to tailor proposals to technology-area priorities and requirements. Topic pages may link to technical priorities, desired outcomes, and partner/industry engagement expectations.
